note.text:
With compound interest, the interest of each year is added to the principal, and the next year's interest is worked out on the new total.
Year 1: interest = r % of P; amount = P + interest. Year 2: interest = r % of the new amount; and so on.
Formula: amount after n years A = P × (1 + r ÷ 100)ⁿ. Compound interest = A − P.
Compound interest is more than simple interest after the first year, because interest is earned on interest.

worked_example.problem: Find the amount after two years on {P} FCFA at {r} % compound interest.
steps: First year: {r} % of {P} = {pctOf(r, P)}; amount {compound(P, r, 1)}.
Second year: {r} % of {compound(P, r, 1)} = {pctOf(r, compound(P, r, 1))}; amount {compound(P, r, 2)}.

cards.idea: Year by year: add each year's interest before working out the next.

check.prompt: Find the compound interest on {P} FCFA at {r} % per year for two years.

misconceptions.explain: That is the amount. The interest is the amount − the principal.
That is simple interest; compound interest adds interest on interest.

solution: Amount after two years: {compound(P, r, 2)} FCFA.

cards.idea: After two years compound beats simple interest.

check.prompt: How much more does {P} FCFA earn in two years at {r} % compound interest than at {r} % simple interest?

misconceptions.explain: That is the compound interest. Take away the simple interest.

solution: Compound: {compound(P, r, 2) - P} FCFA. Simple: {simpleInterest(P, r, 2)} FCFA.

questions.prompt: {P} FCFA is saved at {r} % compound interest. What is the amount after one year?

misconceptions.explain: That is the interest only. Add the principal.

questions.prompt: {P} FCFA is saved at {r} % compound interest. What is the amount after two years?

misconceptions.explain: That is simple interest. With compound interest the second year's interest is on {compound(P, r, 1)}.

solution: After the first year: {compound(P, r, 1)} FCFA.
Second year: {compound(P, r, 1)} + {pctOf(r, compound(P, r, 1))} = {answer} FCFA.
